tells.1: none; at most, it is so evenly trimmed that it feels a little edited-down
tells.2: Upbeat spin and reassurance padding ('Quick heads-up', 'On a happier note', 'you don't have to pay the new price right away')
tells.3: Generic benefit filler: 'so you'll have more options during the week' doesn't fit Sunday classes
tells.4: none; the comma splice, '1st', '/month' and exclamation points read like a real small-business owner
tells.5: Polished template phrasing ('to give you more options during the week', 'Thank you for being part of our community')

reason: Version 4 has the natural rough edges of a gym owner's email, but its comma splice and stiff 'at which time' make it weaker to send. Version 1 states the increase, the grandfathered rate and the new classes plainly, with no spin or filler, so it reads as honest and respectful.
